av_event.line_text: Nobody talks to you. Nobody wants your opinion on the way out. You just sit there for two hours and nothing's your problem.
av_event.what: In the bottom right corner of Rebecca's frame, the brindle lurcher climbs out of the grey dog bed, stretches, and walks across behind Rebecca's chair and out of shot to the left. Rebecca doesn't turn round.

text:
B: Hiya! Hello. Can you hear me?
A: Yeah. Hi.
B: I'm Rebecca, Exeter. Sorry, I'm still in my work fleece, I never get changed.
A: Dominic. Walthamstow. That's fine.
B: What do you do, Dominic?
A: Post-production. I run a company in Soho. Editing, colour, sound, mostly adverts.
B: Oh, fancy. Anything I'd know?
A: There was a fox one. Supermarket, last Christmas.
B: Oh my god, the fox! My mum sent me that about four times. She sort of, kind of sobbed at it. That's you?
A: Me and about fourteen other people. But yeah.
B: That's brilliant. I'm a vet, by the way, farm animals mostly, out near Crediton. Cows, sheep, calvings at three in the morning, that kind of thing.
A: Right. That's sort of the opposite of what I do.
B: How'd you mean?
A: Well, nobody's going to die if a colour grade's a bit off. Clients act like it, but.
B: Ha, yeah. Although honestly, half the time it's not dying, it's just a cow being stubborn in a freezing shed and me being knackered. It's long hours. Fifty, sixty a week, and the out-of-hours on top. Which, sorry, I'm guessing you're the same? You look a bit like I feel.
A: Yeah. Ten till ten when it's busy. I've been told I look tired a lot today.
B: Sorry! It wasn't a criticism. It's a club. The knackered club.
A: [laughs] Fair enough.
B: Do you like it though? Like, actually like it?
A: Er... yeah. Mostly. The edit suite I like. The rest is emails and invoices, and I'm not very good at those. My business partner basically holds it together.
B: Oh, that's me with clinical notes. I do them on the sofa at half ten at night, it's terrible. What do you do to switch off, if you ever do?
A: Cinema. On my own, mostly. Prince Charles, the BFI. Two, three times a week when I can.
B: On your own? I love that. I've never done it. Is it nice?
A: Yeah. Nobody talks to you. Nobody wants your opinion on the way out. You just sit there for two hours and nothing's your problem.
B: Nothing's your problem. God, that sounds amazing. My version is sea swimming at Exmouth. You get in, it's proper cold, and for about five minutes you can't think about anything except how cold it is. Which is kind of the same thing, I suppose, just wetter.
A: I'll stick with the cinema.
B: Everyone says that. Agnieszka told me the sea's for fish.
A: [laughs] I haven't had her yet.
B: Oh, you'll be fine. She's dry, but she's alright. What's the best thing you've seen lately?
A: A Korean thriller, last week. All in one flat. It was alright actually.
B: "Alright actually." Is that London for brilliant?
A: Pretty much.
B: Right, I'm writing it down. Do you ever get people asking you to cut their wedding videos? Because Dan's sister—
